implSummary:
Six commits, one per decision, in the load-bearing D1→D6 order. No commit in the history has the picker reachable without the bank gate.

D1 (74d218f, src/catan_rl/gui/view.py) — took ONLY the `get_resource_selection` hunks from the reference branch ba8f8ac: DISCARD now `bank_recirculate`s, YoP `bank_draw`s gated on `bank_can_supply`, a cancelled partial YoP puts back what it drew, plus the two in-function display hunks (greyed swatch + "(greyed = bank empty)" title suffix) that make the gate visible rather than a silently swallowed click. Explicitly NOT taken: the 1200x900 window resize, `HAND_PANEL_LINE_HEIGHT` 18→20, `MOVE_LOG_RECT` y-shift, the geometry comment rewrites, the engine/board.py resize and the engine_parity re-pin. Test `tests/unit/gui/test_human_picker_bank.py` (247 lines, verbatim from ba8f8ac) was verified RED on the pre-change tree — 4 failed / 3 passed — then green 7/7.

D2 (42c55ec, scripts/play_vs_model.py) — `HumanVsBotEnv.reset` override flips `opponent_player.isAI = False` permanently, plus `_assert_bank_conservation`, `_make_bank_conservation_reporter` (non-fatal, one-shot, carries `.ok`), `check_bank(env)` after reset and after every interactive step, `_assert_bank_conservation` after both self_test step sites, and the `"bank_ok"` record key. Ported `TestHumanSeatIsNotAI` + `TestBankConservationGuard`; verified RED (7 failed) before the code landed.

D3 (6bc0cc2) — deleted `self._human_pre_roll()` and the ~35-line `_human_pre_roll` method (with one of the five `sys.exit(0)` paths); rewrote the `_run_opponent_turn` docstring, which previously advertised the call as "the only addition". Added `"preroll": false` to the record. New `TestNoPreRollWindow` pins the removal AND the parity claim the fairness argument rests on (`compute_action_masks` under `roll_pending` yields exactly `{ROLL_DICE}`, asserted against a live env, not a comment).

D4 (234fb5c) — loop body wrapped in `try/except BaseException` (NOT `Exception`; a test asserts the handler name via AST precisely because `SystemExit`/`KeyboardInterrupt` would slip through), falling through to the existing write block with `partial=True` threaded into `_HumanGameRecorder.finish(..., partial=False)` (new defaulted kwarg, so `recorder_loop`'s caller is unaffected) and an additive `"partial"` JSONL key. `TestCrashSafeArtifacts` drives real `play_interactive` headlessly with an exploding `env.step` and asserts BOTH artifacts land; verified RED first.

D5 (fc6d1a1) — `git_sha` / `ckpt_sha256` appended to `Metadata` after the existing defaulted v2 fields; `REPLAY_SCHEMA_VERSION` deliberately stays 2 (additive-with-default is the precedent `mode`/`sims`/`clairvoyant`/`reveal_bot` set, and `test_the_bump_shipped_with_its_migration` demands a migration for any bump). `_git_sha()` and `_ckpt_sha256()` degrade to `None` — provenance must never stop a game from being played, and `None` means "could not read", never "clean".

D6 (7df9c37) — OPS STEP DONE IN THE OWNER'S MAIN CHECKOUT (runs/ is gitignored): `bank_anchor(runs/train/selfplay_pointer_arch_v2/checkpoints/ckpt_000000500.pt, runs/anchors/ptr_v1_u500.pt)` — 5.6 MB policy-only slim, non-destructive, source untouched. - ORDERING (AC5): `git log main..HEAD` is 74d218f (D1 view.py bank) -> 42c55ec (D2 isAI flip + guard + bank_ok) -> 6bc0cc2 (D3) -> 234fb5c (D4) -> fc6d1a1 (D5) -> 7df9c37 (D6). D1 strictly precedes D2, so no commit exists where the picker is reachable through an ungated grant path.

- RED-FIRST for D1 verified independently, not taken on trust: I extracted main's tree (`git archive main src`) and ran the new `tests/unit/gui/test_human_picker_bank.py` against it — 4 failed / 3 passed, e.g. `assert 19 == 17` on the YoP bank draw. Main's view.py has zero `bank_recirculate`/`bank_draw` calls, confirming the 17/24-card leakage premise.
- NO DOUBLE-COUNTING (the real hazard in D1): `player.play_devCard`'s GUI YoP branch (engine/player.py:466-475) does not add resources itself, and `discardResources` (engine/player.py:628-631) does not decrement — the view is the sole mutator, so adding bank calls there cannot double-count. - D6 ops step verified by content, not by filename: `runs/anchors/ptr_v1_u500.pt`'s `policy_state_dict` hashes byte-identical (sha256 eca7589c51ce9d48…) to `runs/train/selfplay_pointer_arch_v2/checkpoints/ckpt_000000500.pt`. The rotation risk D6 cites is real — that source directory currently holds exactly 6 checkpoints (399/424/449/474/499/500).
- ADDITIVITY (D5): `finish(..., partial: bool = False)` sits after `*` so it is keyword-only with a default; replay metadata reads the two new keys via `.get()`, pinned by `test_a_payload_without_the_attribution_keys_still_loads`. Old readers and old payloads both keep working. Legacy JSONL keys are untouched; every new key is new.
- D4's `except BaseException` is confirmed by AST pin AND by three behavioural tests including the load-bearing `pygame.quit()`-then-`SystemExit` variant. D3's removal is pinned three ways, including a runtime pin that the auto-played human seat never pre-rolls and a pin that masks emit only ROLL_DICE while roll_pending. A missing checkpoint fails loudly in the interactive path (`build_actor` raises FileNotFoundError), so no game can silently be recorded against fresh weights.

The ten findings are all polish on a correct implementation. The two SHOULD-FIXes are both worth a few minutes before tonight: the 120 s post-abort screen hold plus stack-trace on a deliberate window close will read as a hang/crash on the most likely quit path, and the `-dirty` suffix will fire on every record because it counts untracked files that the owner's tree permanently has.

findings.issue: After a D4 salvage abort the driver still falls into `_hold_final_screen()`, which blocks up to FINAL_SCREEN_HOLD_S = 120 s. `_hold_final_screen`'s early return only fires when pygame is torn down, and only ONE of the four quit paths calls `pygame.quit()` before `sys.exit(0)` (scripts/play_vs_model.py:626-627). The three `sys.exit(0)` sites in src/catan_rl/gui/view.py (:407 setup placement, :822 the discard/YoP/Monopoly picker, :994) do NOT, so on the most likely mid-game quit — closing the window while a picker is open — pygame is still initialised, the surface still exists, and the process sits for 120 s after the human already asked to quit. Compounding it, `traceback.print_exc()` at :1686 dumps a full stack trace for a deliberate `SystemExit(0)`, so a normal window-close reads as a crash. Neither is caught by the new tests, which monkeypatch `_hold_final_screen` to a no-op (tests/unit/scripts/test_play_vs_model.py `_run`).
findings.fix: Guard the hold and the traceback on the abort reason: `if not aborted: _hold_final_screen()`, and inside the handler `if not isinstance(exc, SystemExit): traceback.print_exc()`. Drop the `_hold_final_screen` monkeypatch from at least the `tear_down_pygame=False` test so the pin covers the real path.

findings.issue: The `-dirty` suffix is computed from `git status --porcelain` with untracked files included. The owner's main checkout (the tree the games will actually be played from) currently reports `?? $SCRATCH/`, `?? src.mp4`, `?? data/bc/`, `?? data/exit/`, `?? scripts/dev/*.js` plus `M .claude/scheduled_tasks.lock` — none of which change the code the game runs on. Every record written tonight will therefore carry `<sha>-dirty` unconditionally, so the marker distinguishes nothing and `git_sha` stops being a parseable 40-char SHA (the new test itself has to `removesuffix("-dirty")`). D5's stated purpose is attribution; an always-on dirty flag is noise, not attribution. It does match `scripts/bench_engine.py:105-129`, so the convention is defensible in the abstract — but there it annotates a one-off benchmark manifest, not every recorded game.
findings.fix: Use `["git", "status", "--porcelain", "--untracked-files=no"]` so the suffix tracks modifications to *tracked* code, or keep `git_sha` a clean SHA and record dirtiness as a separate additive boolean key.

findings.issue: Neither `subprocess.run` call passes a `timeout`, and only `OSError` is caught — `subprocess.SubprocessError` / `TimeoutExpired` are not. The function's own docstring promises it "degrades to None rather than raising — provenance must never stop a game from being played", but a wedged `git` (index.lock contention, stalled filesystem) would block the artifact write indefinitely. The convention it cites, `bench_engine._git_sha`, passes `timeout=2.0` and catches `(OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired, subprocess.CalledProcessError)`.
findings.fix: Add `timeout=2.0` to both calls and widen the except to `(OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError)`.

findings.issue: The comment claims "five GUI paths call `sys.exit(0)` on `pygame.QUIT`". `grep -rn 'sys.exit(0)' src/catan_rl/gui/ scripts/play_vs_model.py` finds four: view.py:407, view.py:822, view.py:994, play_vs_model.py:627. The number was carried verbatim from the spec prose rather than re-counted against the tree, and the comment is load-bearing (it is the justification for `except BaseException`).
findings.fix: Say "four" (or drop the count and name the files), in the comment at :1668, the docstring at :896-897, and the `TestCrashSafeArtifacts` docstring.

findings.issue: The salvage try/except covers only the `while` loop. `env.reset(seed=..., options={...})` at :1580 drives the human's whole snake-draft placement through the GUI, and view.py:407's QUIT handler `sys.exit(0)`s straight out of it — so closing the window during setup still produces zero artifacts. This is outside D4's literal scope (the spec scopes the fix to the loop and AC7 says "mid-game"), and the loss is ~30 s not an hour, so it is not a spec violation — but the goal statement is "a misclick cannot destroy an hour of play" and this is the one remaining hole.
findings.fix: Optional: extend the same `except BaseException` around the reset + view-construction block, or note the gap in the D4 comment so it is a known limit rather than an oversight.

findings.issue: The AST pin only walks `ast.While` nodes (`isinstance(n, ast.While) and _steps_env(n)`). `self_test` steps the env from a `for _ in range(40):` loop (scripts/play_vs_model.py:1868-1870), which the pin does not see. That loop does call `_assert_bank_conservation` today, but nothing keeps it there — the pin's own docstring argues it exists precisely because the previous text-grep version could pass while the guard sat outside the loop.
findings.fix: Include `ast.For` alongside `ast.While` in the `stepping` comprehension.

findings.issue: Residual capability asymmetry, SPEC-MANDATED — flagging for awareness only, not asking for a change. With a resource fully drained, the human's YoP click is refused and they simply pick something else (a free re-pick), while the policy's YoP at src/catan_rl/env/catan_env.py:611-615 and the AI branch at src/catan_rl/engine/player.py:459-464 burn the pick on an unsupplyable resource. AC4 explicitly requires "a bank-unsupplyable YoP pick is not grantable", and the code comment reasons the case through honestly, so this is the owner's decision implemented as written — but a feature whose headline is FAIR retains one small asymmetry in the human's favour. Reachability is low (requires all 19 of one resource in hands). A related edge: if the bank can supply only one card total, a 2-pick YoP cannot be completed and the human must cancel (the cancel path refunds the card and recirculates correctly, so no corruption).
findings.fix: None required. If you ever want exact parity, grant-what-you-can on confirm instead of refusing the click — but that contradicts AC4, so leave it.

findings.issue: Still describes `_human_pre_roll` as a live code path ("the human's pre-roll knight window (`scripts/play_vs_v8.py:317`, `_human_pre_roll`) fires MOVE_ROBBER / STEAL..."). D3 deleted it. The corresponding test docstring in tests/unit/replay/test_partition_attribution.py WAS updated, so the stale reference is now the only one. CLAUDE.md §6 asks that existing artifacts referencing touched code stay truthful; ratified specs are arguably point-in-time records, which is why this is a NIT and not higher.
findings.fix: Append a one-line superseded-by note pointing at playable-and-recordable.md D3, or leave it if ratified specs are treated as immutable history.

findings.issue: The `git_sha` field docstring says it is "`git rev-parse HEAD` of the tree the game was played on, or None" — it does not mention that the writer can append `-dirty`, so a consumer that assumes a 40-char SHA will be surprised. (`ckpt_sha256`'s docstring is accurate.)
findings.fix: Add: "may carry a `-dirty` suffix when the tree had uncommitted edits."
None in this diff. Worth knowing that any future `--self-test` gate step in a worktree should force `PYTHONPATH` (or give the worktree its own venv) or its PASS names the wrong tree.

FINDINGS: no BLOCKER. Four SHOULD-FIXes — one truth-drift item where the `_no_pre_roll` rationale claims MCTS clones need it (they structurally cannot reach the branch; I measured 0 calls during a real search on the pre-change tree), a `-dirty` suffix that will be unconditionally ON in the owner's checkout tonight because it counts untracked files and `.claude/scheduled_tasks.lock` (measured: `-dirty` with `src/` byte-clean), the schema docstring not documenting that suffix, and the ratified spec file itself not being committed while all 12 siblings are. findings.issue: Truth drift — the justification for the `_no_pre_roll` suppression asserts something the tree disproves. The comment says the base env's `heuristic_pre_roll` fires on "EVERY MCTS clone rollout and every --self-test game". `search/mcts.py:166` (`clone_env`) always ends with `clone.set_snapshot_opponent(opponent)` and `search/agent.py:79` always builds a non-None `FrozenSnapshotOpponent`, while `env/catan_env.py:804` gates the pre-roll on `self._snapshot_opponent is None`. So the pre-roll can NEVER fire in an MCTS clone. I confirmed this empirically against the pre-change tree (pristine `main` extracted to a scratch dir): `heuristic_pre_roll calls DURING one search: 0`. The code change is harmless and correct for the path it actually covers (`--self-test` / any headless `HumanVsBotEnv`), but the stated reason — "the bot would search against a human who can pre-roll" — is false, and it is now repeated in a code comment, a test docstring and CLAUDE.md. A false rationale in three places is exactly the kind of claim a later reader will build on.
findings.fix: Rewrite the comment, the `test_the_auto_played_human_seat_never_pre_rolls` docstring and the CLAUDE.md sentence to say what is true: the suppression covers `--self-test` and any headless `HumanVsBotEnv` auto-play; MCTS clones already skip the pre-roll because `clone_env` always attaches a `SnapshotOpponent` and `catan_env.py:804` gates on `_snapshot_opponent is None`.

findings.issue: The `-dirty` suffix is unconditionally ON in practice, so D5's attribution key carries no information. `git status --porcelain` with no path filter and default `-unormal` counts untracked files and every tracked path in the repo. Measured against the owner's actual checkout right now: `would record: 3612e3fa86efcd76ae465ed5a45a2bb407215ea0-dirty` while `src/ dirty? False`. The dirt is `.claude/scheduled_tasks.lock` (a scheduler lockfile the loop itself churns), `scripts/dev/review_step6_plan_wf.js`, plus untracked `src.mp4` / `data/bc/` / `data/exit/`. Every game recorded tonight will be stamped `-dirty` regardless of whether a single line of game-affecting code differs, which defeats the whole point of the key ("the record must name the exact code it was played against").
findings.fix: Scope the dirty probe to code that can affect a game — `git status --porcelain -- src scripts crates configs` — or at minimum pass `--untracked-files=no`. Update the `_git_sha` docstring and the CLAUDE.md `-dirty` sentence to state exactly which paths the flag covers.

findings.issue: Schema doc drift: `Metadata.git_sha`'s docstring says it is "``git rev-parse HEAD`` of the tree the game was played on, or ``None``" — it does not mention that the writer can append `-dirty`, making the value 45 chars instead of 40. This is a shared, versioned contract read by replay consumers; the slice's own test had to add `sha.removesuffix("-dirty")` to keep its length assertion, which is the tell. A consumer that slices or compares against a 40-char SHA silently mismatches.
findings.fix: Add one sentence to the `git_sha` docstring documenting the `-dirty` suffix and its meaning, so the dataclass is the source of truth for the format.

findings.issue: The ratified spec that governs this slice is not on the branch. All 12 sibling specs are tracked (`git ls-files .claude/veriloop/specs/` lists `preroll-dev-cards-r1.md`, `bc-coverage-and-bank-legality.md`, `human-devcard-picker-and-bank.md`, …), but `playable-and-recordable.md` exists only as an untracked file in the owner's main checkout and is absent from the worktree entirely. The code comments cite `preroll-dev-cards-r1.md` by filename, so a reader following the trail will find the stopgap's successor but not the spec that authorised the stopgap.
findings.fix: Commit `.claude/veriloop/specs/playable-and-recordable.md` with this slice, matching the existing convention.

findings.issue: Artifact asymmetry: `git_sha`, `ckpt_sha256` and `partial` reach BOTH the JSONL record and the replay `Metadata`, but `bank_ok` and `preroll` land only in the JSONL. A downstream consumer that reads replay JSON (the richer, schema-versioned artifact) has no way to see that a game's finite-bank invariant broke. Spec D2/D3 only asked for the record key, so this is spec-conformant — but the stated purpose ("a corrupt game must never be byte-indistinguishable from a clean one") is only half-served.
findings.fix: Optional and out of scope for this slice: mirror `bank_ok` / `preroll` into `Metadata` as additive optional fields the same way `git_sha` was, or note the JSONL-only scope in the spec's known limitations.

findings.issue: `TestBankConservationGuard`'s docstring opens with "D3: the human driver asserts the finite-bank invariant it never had." In the ratified spec the conservation guard is D2; D3 is the pre-roll removal. Mis-labelled decision IDs make the acceptance-criteria trace harder to follow.
findings.fix: Change `D3:` to `D2:` in the class docstring.

findings.issue: `_git_sha()` and `_ckpt_sha256(ckpt)` are each evaluated twice per finished game — once for the replay `Metadata`, once for the JSONL record. `_ckpt_sha256` streams the whole checkpoint (the banked anchor is 5.5 MB) and `_git_sha` shells out to git twice each time. Harmless, but it also means the two artifacts could in principle disagree if the tree changed between the two calls.
findings.fix: Compute both once before the write block and reuse the values for both artifacts.

findings.issue: D4's salvage covers the stepping loop only. With `--human-seat 0` the human's snake-draft placements are driven inside `env.reset()`, which sits OUTSIDE the try — a window close during setup still produces no artifact at all. This matches the spec exactly (D4 scopes the wrap to the loop body), so it is not a defect; recording the residual hole so it is a known limitation rather than an assumption that a misclick can never lose a game.
findings.fix: None required for this slice. If it matters later, hoist the reset into the same salvage scope, or note in the spec that setup-phase interruptions are still unrecoverable.

findings.issue: The AST pin only inspects `ast.While` nodes that contain a `.step(` call. `self_test`'s first stepping loop is a `for _ in range(40):` and is therefore invisible to the pin, even though it does call `_assert_bank_conservation` today. A future regression that drops the guard from that loop would not turn the pin red.
findings.fix: Widen the node filter to `(ast.While, ast.For)`.

findings.issue: That spec is still headed "Status: DRAFT (2026-07-29) — awaiting owner ratification" and describes the same re-slice this branch implements (its D1 ordering rationale is the one the ratified spec restates). Leaving a superseded draft in-tree marked as pending invites a later reader to implement its extra decisions (engine re-pin discussion, clause-(a) recording, leak-era voiding) as if they were open.
findings.fix: Mark it SUPERSEDED by `playable-and-recordable.md`, or delete it.
